_guarded_by: test/tool-emulation.test.js — 'normalizeMessagesForCascade — native structured path interleaves parallel tool history' (call-site shape + the emulation-path control) and 'native history assembles to an interleaved role sequence on the wire' (the encoded #2 role bytes).
_ci_observation_2026_09_13: First real CI run (PR #269, Linux, Node 24) reported for mutation 2: 'baseline 72, mutated 70 — a failure from a truncated or load-broken suite is not mutation evidence'. Reproduced locally on Windows: the SAME mutation keeps all 72 assertions running (pass=66 fail=6) and reddens the emulation control. So the truncation is harness-side, not a property of the mutation — but mutate-verify's refusal to score it is right, and it is recorded here rather than argued away. If CI keeps reporting a shrunken run for that mutation, treat it as NOT VERIFIED there and rely on mutation 1, which is narrower.

mutations.name: call site removed — the normalizer stops interleaving parallel tool history, so a batched assistant turn encodes as consecutive role=2 frames and upstream 500/529s the whole session (the defect PR #261 fixes)
interleave runs unconditionally — the native-only gate is dropped, so prompt-emulation history gets restructured too and the emulation control shape changes under every non-native dialect

KNOWN SURVIVOR — a repeated tool_call_id is still split into two assistant frames with the same id (probe 2026-09-13: assistant[c1] / tool(c1) / assistant[c1]). Not covered by design: these tests pin the shape the upstream state machine needs, not OpenAI's uniqueness rule. Deduping would change behaviour for a malformed-history case with no capture behind it.
